description: Edge-case evaluation set for field-level citation generation. Each item names one JSON Pointer in a case result.json, tags the edge cases it exercises, states the expected behaviour, and carries ground-truth anchors (in citations/v1 Anchor shapes) split into acceptable / secondary / forbidden. See eval/README.md for matching and scoring rules.

expectations.cite: At least `minAcceptableMatches` (default 1) `acceptable` evidence entries must be matched by a produced citation whose matching anchor has role `value` (or no role). If that evidence also has label or context anchors, the same citation must cover one of them — the words around the value, not the value string alone. When `requiredContext` is present, at least `minRequiredContextMatches` (default 1) entries must also be matched by produced anchors explicitly marked role `context`. Matching `forbidden` evidence is a false positive.
expectations.context-only: The value is defaulted, derived, or rule-generated. Pass if the produced list is empty OR every produced anchor matches an `acceptable`/`secondary` entry (any role). Any anchor with role `value` that is not matched, or any `forbidden` match, fails.
expectations.empty: Expected output is `[]`. Pass if no produced citation has a `value`-role anchor. `label`/`context` anchors that match `acceptable` entries are tolerated. Any `forbidden` match fails.

categories.multi-citation: The same value is supported by two or more independent locations (often across file types). Recall over `acceptable` is tracked.
categories.multi-box: One piece of evidence spans several OCR words / text segments (first + last name, two dates joined by "to"). Expect one anchor with merged box(es), not a union rectangle over unrelated text.
categories.name: Person or company name.
categories.name:partial: Result holds part of a name (first or last only); the ideal box covers only that word.
categories.normalization:date: Source and result use different date formats (ISO vs US, zero-padding, long-form month).
categories.normalization:currency: Source is a bare number or has cents; result is "$1,234".
categories.normalization:type: Source is a number, result is a string (or vice versa).
categories.normalization:composite: Result is assembled from two or more source strings.
categories.context:required: A correct value citation must be accompanied by a role=context anchor establishing the relevant source section.
categories.list-empty: Result value is `[]`; expected citation list is empty.
categories.list-row-disambiguation: Sibling rows share the identical value; the citation must land in the right row's section.
categories.zero:real: The 0 / $0.00 is literally printed in the source. Must be cited.
categories.zero:default: The 0 / $0 comes from an "if empty display 0" rule; no source cell exists. Must NOT be cited to a random zero.
categories.zero:null-source: The 0 comes from a source field that is explicitly null. The null is the evidence (context role).
categories.zero:derived: The 0 is computed (e.g. count of Open rows); the evidence is the column the count was taken from.
categories.spreadsheet:zeros-everywhere: The source row/table is full of 0 cells (the "premiums are 0 in every row" trap).
categories.blank:absent: Result is "" because the field does not exist in any source document.
categories.blank:present-empty: Result is "" because the field exists in the source but has no value (address line 2 of a one-line address).
categories.blank:by-design: Result is "" because a parent flag is false, so the sub-field is intentionally blank.
categories.constant:rule: Result is a literal constant ("N/A") emitted by a rule in the field definition; the evidence is whatever triggers the rule.
categories.boolean:label-presence: Boolean defined as "label is followed by a non-empty string".
categories.boolean:from-boolean: Boolean supported by a boolean field in a JSON source.
categories.inferred: Value is not printed verbatim; it follows from two facts in the source.
categories.many-occurrences: The value appears many times and every occurrence satisfies the field definition (for example each one is explicitly labeled). Tracks dedupe and cost. An exact string hit that fails the definition is a distractor, not another acceptable citation.
categories.pointer:special-chars: JSON Pointer contains spaces, %, or & in keys.
categories.offsets:utf16-surrogates: The source string contains non-BMP characters (emoji etc.) before the span, so UTF-16 code-unit offsets differ from code-point offsets.
categories.ocr-artifact-for-non-pdf: An *-ocr.json exists for a non-PDF source; page-region anchors on it would be schema-invalid (file must be a PDF).
categories.cross-file-type: The same value is in two different file types.
categories.distractor:same-label-other-table: The same label appears in another table with a different (wrong) number.
categories.distractor:same-value-other-field: The identical string is also the value of a different field.
categories.distractor:same-value-other-column: The identical cell value sits in a neighbouring column of the same row.
categories.distractor:derived-artifact: A downstream artifact (model-check CSV, reconciliation JSON, request or line-selection copy) restates the result. Corroboration at best — citing it alone is not a pass.
categories.distractor:duplicate-header: A CSV has two columns with the same header text.
categories.distractor:near-miss-line-item: A line item is similar to, but does not satisfy, the field definition.
categories.distractor:adjacent-date: Another date (loss date, received date) sits next to where the blank field would be.
categories.distractor:adjacent-field: A neighbouring field (Year Built) holds a plausible-looking value for the blank field.
categories.distractor:same-name-wrong-context: The same person's name appears elsewhere under a different role or in unrelated metadata.
categories.file:email-json: Email exported as JSON; text-span with `pointer` into a string field.
categories.file:txt: Plain-text source; text-span anchors on raw file offsets.
categories.file:eml: RFC 822 email file; text-span anchors on raw offsets (CRLF preserved).
categories.file:html: HTML email body; text-span anchors on raw markup offsets.
categories.file:xlsx-second-sheet: Evidence is on a worksheet other than the first.
categories.distractor:exact-match-wrong-context: The identical string occurs again, but not in the section, page, source, or role the field definition names. Citing it is a false positive.
